newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK business lobby urges govt to boost land supply.
newsitem.headline: HK business lobby urges govt to boost land supply.

text.p: The Hong Kong General Chamber of Commerce called on the government to increase the land supply for luxury residential properties to curb rising prices.
Prices for luxury residential homes have jumped recently, sparking concerns that could lead to a rise in the territory's property market in general.

James Tien, the business lobby's chairman, said in a statement the chamber was primarily concerned with residential property over HK$20 million in price and the band wagon effect that rapid price movement in this category may have on the rest of the residential market if left unchecked for another year.

"The government should use the opportunity to remind the public of the substantial mass market stock of private sector housing which will come on stream during the next three years as MTRC (Mass Transit Railway) station sites are developed," he said.

Tien also called on the government not to further impose administrative measures to keep a lid on the property price as it would only create more problems, and to take a look at the bureaucracy of the land development process.
